title: AEGS test vector
description: One input, one expected output, and the normative clause it checks. The clause is required: a vector without one is a test of somebody's implementation rather than of this specification.

id.description: `<family>/<name>`, matching the file path. Checked against the path by tools/check_vectors.py, because an id that disagrees with its filename makes a failure report point at the wrong file.

clause.description: The normative clause this vector checks. A clause identifier. A lowercase suffix (VERD-4a) inserts a clause without renumbering its neighbours, which matters because renumbering breaks every existing citation -- in the vectors, in the conformance cases, and anywhere outside this repository.

operation.description: A closed set. A vector naming an operation no implementation is required to expose cannot be run, and an unrunnable vector is worse than an absent one because it looks like coverage.

note.description: Why this vector exists, when that is not self-evident. Used heavily for vectors that exist because something once went wrong.

amount.description: A decimal amount, ALWAYS as a string, including for integers. A vector writing 2.5 as a JSON number would have lost precision before any implementation read it — which would make this suite unable to test the very thing ARITH-9 requires.

atomic.description: A count of atomic units. An integer here is safe: that is the point of ARITH-1.

decimals.description: The asset's precision. A property of the asset, not of this specification.

limit.description: Atomic units, or null for an ABSENT limit. Null and 0 are opposite instructions and MUST NOT be conflated -- see ENV-8.

cumulative.description: False for a per-call ceiling: checked fresh against every action, nothing accumulates. A per-call ceiling MUST NOT report a consumed amount -- see ENV-4.

items.description: A count envelope constrains occurrences, not amounts. Evaluated against the count already recorded, independent of the amount being decided -- see ENV-7.

channel.description: Which channel this action belongs to.

limit.description: Atomic units, or null for an ABSENT limit. Null and 0 are opposite instructions and MUST NOT be conflated -- see ENV-8.

cumulative.description: False for a per-call ceiling: checked fresh against every action, nothing accumulates. A per-call ceiling MUST NOT report a consumed amount -- see ENV-4.

otherChannel.description: The opposite channel's state. Present only in vectors checking that channels never share an envelope -- ENV-9.

repeat.description: Perform the action this many times in succession. Used to show that a per-call ceiling does not accumulate.

amountAtomic.description: An amount already in atomic units. An integer here is safe by construction -- that is what ARITH-1 buys. Distinct from `amount`, which is a decimal string because ARITH-9 requires one.

standing.description: The verdict already reached before these proposals are applied. Null where no rule matched at all.

standingControl.description: Which control produced the standing verdict. Needed by VERD-5: if nothing narrows, attribution falls to whatever decided, and an implementation attributing only refusals has records that go quiet when an auditor asks why something was allowed.

proposals.description: Controls' proposals, IN EVALUATION ORDER. Order does not affect the final verdict (VERD-3) and does affect attribution (VERD-4), which is the asymmetry this family exists to pin down.

verdict.description: Null means NO OPINION, which is not approval. A control with nothing to say must not vote APPROVE, or a silent control looks like an endorsing one.

recordsEvidence.description: Whether this control leaves a trace in the record. VERD-6 requires evidence that a control RAN, independently of whether it changed the verdict.

noRuleMatched.description: No policy rule matched the action. VERD-8 requires that this not approve.

advisorUnavailable.description: The advisory model could not be reached. VERD-9 requires the decision not to depend on its availability.

dispositive.description: Controls declared dispositive: the finding determines attribution whenever present, whether or not it narrowed the verdict. VERD-4a requires the set and its precedence to be DOCUMENTED -- an undeclared dispositive control is indistinguishable from arbitrary attribution.

usd.description: Plain decimal, never exponent notation. Some languages format 0.000001 as 1e-06 — the same number and a different hash.

reason.description: A CATEGORY, not a message. An implementation's wording is its own business; a vector checks that it refused for the right kind of reason. Matching exact strings would make this suite a test of one implementation's vocabulary, which is precisely what a conformance suite must not be.

breached.description: EVERY envelope the amount exceeds, not merely the first. Order is not significant; an implementation may report them in any order.

binding.description: The envelope whose breach determined the refusal. MUST be null when nothing was breached -- see ENV-6.

tightest.description: The envelope with the least headroom, whether or not anything was breached. A different question from `binding`, and most useful when nothing has been refused.

headroom.description: Expected headroom per envelope name, floored at zero.

used.description: Expected consumed amount per envelope name. Null asserts that no consumed amount is reported, which is what ENV-4 requires of a per-call ceiling.

verdictNot.description: The verdict MUST NOT be this. Used where AEGS constrains the outcome without fixing it -- VERD-8 forbids approving an unmatched action without dictating which non-approving verdict to use.

attributedControl.description: The last control that narrowed. Null asserts that NONE of the proposals narrowed -- not that attribution is absent, which VERD-5 forbids.

evidenced.description: Controls that must have left evidence they ran.
